newsitem.title: USA: Bank earnings fell to $13.2 bln in third quarter. [CORRECTED 17:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Bank earnings fell to $13.2 bln in third quarter. [CORRECTED 17:55 GMT]

text.p: U.S commercial banks earned $13.2 billion in the third quarter, down five percent from the $13.8 billion earned in the same period last year, Federal Deposit Insurance Corp reported Friday.

Nearly all of the decline came from $1 billion in one-time special assessments levied on banks for the Savings Association Insurance Fund. The assessments lowered after-tax net income by $650 million, the FDIC said.
Even after the contributions, third quarter bank earnings were the third highest quarterly total ever, FDIC said.
Although the credit quality of most types of bank loans improved in the quarter, the quality of consumer loans and especially credit card loans declined, FDIC said.
Credit card loan charge-offs accounted for almost two-thirds of the $3.8 billion of net loan charge-offs for the quarter, FDIC said.

Annualized charge-off rate for credit card loans was 4.41 percent, down slightly from the 4.49 percent reported in the second quarter of this year. The rate declined even though the amount of charge-offs increased because the amount of total outstanding credit card loans grew even faster, FDIC said.

The total amount of credit card lending, including commitments to consumers that have not yet been tapped, rose to $1.6 trillion (corrects from billion) in the third quarter from $1.4 trillion (corrects from billion) in the same period last year. The figures also included credit card receivables that banks have securitized.

FDIC chairman Ricki Helfer downplayed concerns about the credit card sector, however. "I think the credit card lending problem is a problem we have to continue to monitor," Helfer said at a press conference here. "Does this mean it is a significant problem area for the banking industry? No, but it is an area that we have to continue to monitor."
Average return on assets, a key measure of profitability, for banks specializing in credit card lending has declined but remained higher than the overall average return for all banks, Helfer noted.

"Returns on assets was 2.02 percent at credit card banks, still well above the average for the industry as a whole of 1.19 percent," Helfer said. "If these banks can effectively monitor the risk and price the cost of credit card lending in such a way as to offset the losses, it shouldn't create significant safety and soundness problems."
